about: A known chain of hand-offs: three processes in a ring of pipes pass a token around a known number of laps. Each hand-off is one wakeup, from the process that wrote to the one that was blocked reading, and nothing else in the program wakes anyone.

trust.count: an upper bound, reached on an idle machine: one write to a pipe a blocked reader waits on is one wakeup of that reader, and each relay holds the token for `hold_us` on the cpu before passing it so that the next is asleep when the byte arrives. On a loaded machine a reader can still be runnable when the byte comes, and that hand-off wakes nobody: 266 of 300 were seen with nine test runs sharing the machine. The direction is exact: no edge goes the other way
trust.chain: the chain is a ring: a -> b -> c -> a, and no edge goes the other way
